title: Research: how SRS is used and what it needs

sections.name: intro
sections.label: Introduction
sections.content:
This is where the programme studies SRS in use: what it needs, how work moves, and how a repository should be structured. Each thread follows one question and is written as a tree of documents: an overview first, then parts, then the evidence. Start with the overview of the thread you need, and go one level deeper only when you need more.

The owner, 2026-10-30: "Where we have a research area it should be structured as a tree of documents that get deeper. As a human or agent I should be able to find a top level introduction and then drill down into parts."

sections.name: threads
sections.label: The threads
sections.content:
- Readable repositories, tested: the core offering, a set of checks, the audits of our corpora, and the issue list of quick wins, big wins and tool fixes.
- Open exercises: every open question in Research and on the session agenda, kept as a question with options to explore before it becomes a decision.
- The graph: why SRS needs a graph element. The evidence supports one-hop selection by relation, visible links and a bounded walk in the core, not a query language.
- Human-readable repositories: how a repository is structured for people. Five parts, from the front door to how we test readability.
- Affirmation and confidence: where human judgement belongs. Affirmation by fork has become a sink (304 of 313 affirmed records are copies); the move is to confidence built from relationships, with an optional human tip.
- Dreamtime: long-term memory as a practice. Dreams that test our data in scenarios, keep the readable hierarchy in shape, and strengthen relationships when storylines recur.
- Flow and decisions: the models of how work moves and how decisions settle.
- The domain map: where the work happens, from the base domain down to the stages of the flow.

sections.name: practice
sections.label: How a thread works
sections.content: A thread is a section with an overview document: the claim, the story the evidence tells, the parts, and the open questions. It is rewritten as the evidence changes, never appended to as a log. Each part is a document of its own, holding its evidence below it. Existing records join by membership and are never copied. New evidence becomes a finding in Suggestions that evidences the problem it bears on. Owner words enter first as vignettes in their conversation container. Counter-evidence stays in the same thread: a thread that only collects support is advocacy, not research.

sections.name: find
sections.label: How to find it
sections.content: Each thread and part is its own section. srs find --container <section> searches that section's direct members only, so search a part's section to reach its evidence (searching a thread reaches its part documents). Every open question is an exercise: srs find --type governance/exercise --tag research --text "<term>". srs-context points here (convention a752700b, in its Brief).
